screenSummary.playArea: A top-down view of the solar system from above Earth's north pole. Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn move counter-clockwise on circular orbits around the Sun.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose to view the inner planets or all planets, show speed arrows and labels, read the orbital data table, and play, pause or change the speed of time.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Press play and compare how fast the inner and outer planets move.

orbits.currentDetailsPattern: Elapsed time {{years}} years. Mercury moves at {{mercury}} km/s and Saturn at {{saturn}} km/s: planets farther from the Sun move more slowly.

screenSummary.playArea: A top-down view with the Sun at the center, Earth fixed below it, and one hypothetical planet on a circular orbit. Lines from Earth point to the Sun and to the planet; the angle between them is the elongation.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a superior or inferior planet, set its orbit radius, and show sight lines, the elongation angle, the east and west sides of the sky, and where each named configuration lies.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the planet around its orbit and watch the elongation and configuration name change.

configurations.currentDetailsPattern: The {{type}} planet is at {{elongation}}. Configuration: {{configuration}}. In Earth's sky it is {{sky}}.

controls.planetHelp: Use the arrow keys to move the planet along its orbit.
controls.eastWestSides: Shade the east and west sides

screenSummary.playArea: A top-down view of the observer's and target planet's orbits around the Sun. Below it, a strip of zodiac constellations shows where the Sun and target appear in the observer's sky, with a trail of the target's recent path.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose the observer's and target planets, read the counter, elongation, current and next configuration and direction of motion, jump between configurations, choose where to pause, and control time.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move a planet to a configuration, zero the counter, then play until the same configuration returns.

synodic.currentDetailsPattern: Observer {{observer}}, target {{target}}. Counter {{elapsed}}. Elongation {{elongation}}. Configuration: {{configuration}}. Motion is {{motion}}.

controls.planetHelp: Use the arrow keys to move this planet along its orbit; time changes to match.
controls.pauseAtStationary: Pause at the start and end of retrograde motion

screenSummary.playArea: A graph of synodic period against distance from the Sun for planets seen from Earth. The synodic period grows without limit near Earth's orbit and approaches one year far from it.
screenSummary.controlArea: A calculator converts between synodic and sidereal periods for inferior and superior planets. A hypothetical planet can be moved along the graph.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Enter a synodic period you measured and read the sidereal period.

periods.currentDetailsPattern: Calculator: {{input}} gives {{result}}. Hypothetical planet at {{a}} AU has sidereal period {{p}} years and synodic period {{s}} years.

controls.markerHelp: Use the arrow keys to move the planet closer to or farther from the Sun.

screenSummary.playArea: Ptolemy's Earth-centered model. The planet moves on a small circle, the epicycle, whose center moves on a larger circle, the deferent, around Earth. Below, a zodiac strip shows the planet's path against the stars.
screenSummary.controlArea: Choose a planet preset, adjust the epicycle size, eccentricity, motion rate and apogee angle, choose what to show, and control time.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Press play and watch the planet loop backward against the stars.

ptolemaic.currentDetailsPattern: {{planet}} at ecliptic longitude {{longitude}} degrees, moving {{motion}}. Elapsed time {{days}} days.
